insight.title: Northbridge Athletic Repeatedly Attacks Through Right Channel
insight.canonical_claim: Northbridge Athletic made 10 of their last 11 final-third entries through the right channel in the last 10 minutes, across 8 possessions, with 1 entry reaching the box or producing a shot.
insight.why_it_matters: This pattern shows a strong preference for attacking down the right side, which could influence defensive focus and game dynamics.
insight.uncertainty: This does not establish tactical intent, defensive positioning effects, or predict future outcomes.

observed_facts.statement: 10 of Northbridge Athletic's last 11 final-third entries came through the right channel in the last 10 minutes, across 8 separate possessions.
One of these entries reached the box or produced a shot, which resulted in a goal by player #9 N. Vantreight at 28'.

The passes and carries involved in these entries were predominantly completed by players #4 M. Lindqvist, #7 K. Rennard, #2 D. Mensah-Lowe, and #9 N. Vantreight, with many passes ending near the right channel coordinates.

match_context: Northbridge Athletic is the home team attacking in the +x direction.
Both teams have 11 players on the pitch.
alternative_explanations: The repeated entries through the right channel could be due to player positioning or opponent defensive weaknesses rather than a deliberate tactical plan.
The shot resulting from the right channel entry might be coincidental rather than a direct consequence of the repeated channel attacks.
cannot_establish: Whether defenders were dragged, pulled, or caught out of position due to these attacks (no tracking data).
